To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) self‐disorders were associated with a higher likelihood of a lifetime diagnosis of schizophrenia‐spectrum disorder; 2) this association was independent of other premorbid symptoms and of a family history of schizophrenia; and 3) the association of self‐disorder with schizophrenia‐spectrum diagnosis was strongest for patients with the most severe premorbid symptoms, suggesting that self‐disorder is a particularly important vulnerability factor in the most severe cases of schizophrenia.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
self‐disorder is not only a marker for schizophrenia but also for other psychotic and non‐psychotic disorders.
self‐disorder is a valid construct for predicting later schizophrenia and related diagnoses, even in a non‐clinical sample.
the EASE is a valid, reliable and useful tool for identifying individuals with a premorbid vulnerability to schizophrenia.
